Landlord Joe Sanders says there have been a number of mysterious incidents

Neil Shaw Assistant Editor

13:03, 25 Sep 2026Updated 13:08, 25 Sep 2026

CCTV caaught moment glass flew from shelf in 'haunted' pub

The landlord of a 'haunted' pub claims footage of a glass jumping off the shelf onto the bar could be the ghost of a thirsty customer 'wanting a pint'. Joe Sanders and his wife Sarah have owned the Red Lion Inn in Sturminster Marshall near Wimborne, Dorset, for five years and said they've noticed strange things happening around the bar.

‌

The couple shared CCTV footage of the glass crashing down onto the bar on Facebook captioned, 'Every pub has a ghost, especially one as old as ours. They clearly wanted a pint'. The clip shows a glass apparently hurling itself off the shelf above the bar and crashing down onto the bar. Puzzled Sarah, who was putting another glass away, can be seen looking up in a bid to find where the mystery missile came from, as one customer looked on in shock.

‌

‌

Sarah, 54, then showed the footage to husband Joe, 50, who believes it could be a ghostly customer visiting who simply wants a pint. Joe, said: "I was upstairs, my wife was at the counter and she showed me the video on the CCTV. It nearly hit her. It didn't break either, which is weird.

‌

"There's been a running joke with glasses falling, normally from the bottom shelf and we just thought they're badly put away. Things in the kitchen have gone flying off before [it's] very random. This is the first time we've actually seen it.

"When you look at it, it kind of looks like it jumps. We live right opposite a churchyard and there's always that joke about that [as] we're only across the road. Lots of people thought we have a poltergeist, it was actually quite weird. Maybe it could be an old customer, he clearly wanted a pint."

Article continues below

Joe admits he thought perhaps glasses were being put away awkwardly, which was causing them to fall, but after seeing the video he says it simply 'pops off'.

Joe said: "I'm certainly not worried. It doesn't bother me [...] everything seems to happen around the bar. It's weird. We can't believe the glass didn't break, it bounced off the bar and on the floor.

"Everyone I show it to says it's just bizarre, you zoom in on the glass and see it pop off. I think customers are more interested than freaked out. I'm not really spooked by it."
